sections.title: I. Macroeconomic Developments
sections.description: GDP growth, inflation, exchange rate, monetary policy, fiscal position, key industry performance

events.title: BCP raises 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5%, lowers inflation projection to 3.3% (2026-07-15)
events.summary: The Central Bank of Paraguay (BCP) released its July Monetary Policy Report (IPoM), upgrading the 2026 GDP growth forecast from 4.2% to 4.5%, driven by record soybean harvest, stronger manufacturing (oils & chemicals), and dynamic services. Sectoral revisions: agriculture 4.7% (from 3.2%), manufacturing 4.6% (from 4.1%), electricity & water 7.4% (from 5.7%). Livestock was cut to 0.1% due to herd retention. The BCP simultaneously lowered its end-2026 inflation forecast from 3.5% to 3.3%, with core inflation (IPCSAE) revised down from 3.1% to 2.8%. June YoY inflation stood at just 2.09%. The EVE survey of market agents, however, maintained more conservative projections: 4.2% GDP growth and 3.5% inflation.

events.title: Moody's affirms Paraguay's Baa3 investment grade for third consecutive year, outlook stable (2026-07-17)
events.summary: Moody's Ratings affirmed Paraguay's sovereign credit rating at Baa3 with a stable outlook for the third consecutive year since the initial upgrade in July 2024. Paraguay now holds double investment grade (Moody's Baa3 and S&P BBB-), with Fitch at BB+ (one notch below). Moody's highlighted Paraguay's robust economic growth, low and stable public debt (~41% of GDP), and credible monetary policy. Key challenges cited include limited government revenue base (14% of GDP tax pressure), high proportion of foreign-currency debt exposing the country to FX volatility, and structural dependence on agriculture and hydroelectricity. FDI reached a record USD 1,180 million in 2025 per ECLAC data.

events.title: Market agents cut exchange rate forecasts: end-2026 revised down to PYG 6,300/USD (2026-07-17)
events.summary: The BCP's July EVE survey shows market agents revised down exchange rate projections across all horizons: July 2026 at PYG 6,100 (from 6,200), August at 6,150, end-2026 at 6,300 (from 6,393), and end-2027 at 6,500. The BCP official rate on July 17 stood at PYG 6,060.78 per USD. The guaraní has appreciated ~8.5% YTD against the dollar, driven by robust agro-export inflows, ample financial system liquidity, and global dollar weakness. The BCP held its policy rate at 5.50% for the fourth consecutive month, with the next meeting scheduled for July 23. The real ex-ante rate of 2.0% remains within the neutral range (1.3%–2.6%). Private-sector credit grew 15.3% YoY and deposits 18.5% YoY as of May 2026.

events.title: Net international reserves at USD 11,329M as of July 10, down from USD 11,505M on July 3 (2026-07-10)
events.summary: Paraguay's net international reserves (RIN) stood at USD 11,329.01 million as of July 10, 2026, according to preliminary BCP data. This represents a decrease of USD 175.8 million from USD 11,504.83 million on July 3. The decline was primarily driven by a reduction in 'Other reserve assets' from USD 9,891.9M to USD 9,726.6M, partially offset by gold holdings at USD 1,087.1M and SDR holdings at USD 451.7M. Year-to-date reserves have shown strong accumulation from USD 10,961M in January to a peak of USD 11,720M in March, followed by gradual moderation. The reserve position remains robust, covering approximately 8 months of imports and providing a strong external buffer.

events.title: DNIT tax revenue grew only 2.1% in H1 2026 vs. 9% budgeted target; President Peña orders intensified H2 collection (2026-07-11)
events.summary: Paraguay's tax authority DNIT reported H1 2026 revenue growth of only 2.1%, significantly below the 9% target budgeted for the full year. President Santiago Peña ordered intensified collection efforts for H2 to close the gap. The IMF's Article IV consultation (June 29) had already warned that the fiscal deficit will exceed the 1.5% GDP target due to regularization of accumulated domestic arrears, including USD 220M to construction firms and approximately USD 1B to the pharmaceutical sector. The IMF projects convergence to the 1.5% deficit target only by 2028 and called for full transparency in public accounts. Public spending grew 11.7% cumulatively in H1 2026.

sections.title: II. Political & Policy Developments
sections.description: Major legislation, policy adjustments, foreign investment regulation, tax reform, investment incentives

events.title: Congress requests reports on tech investment incentives and critical minerals development strategy (2026-07-16)
events.summary: The Chamber of Deputies approved two resolution projects requesting the Executive Branch to report on: (1) MITIC's plan for incentives, infrastructure feasibility, investment mapping, and roadmap to attract high-energy-demand and technology-based companies (data centers, cloud computing, AI), leveraging Paraguay's clean hydroelectric energy; and (2) the Vice-Ministry of Mines and Energy's information on concessions, geological map updates, strategic investment plan, and legislative reforms for the development of lithium, titanium, uranium, and other strategic minerals, including updating the Mining Code (Law 3180/07) on tax incentives, royalties, and exploitation timelines.

events.title: President Peña rules out new energy decrees, delegates tariff decisions to ANDE during Aña Cuá visit (2026-07-17)
events.summary: During a site visit to the Aña Cuá expansion project (Yacyretá, 76% completion), President Santiago Peña stated the Executive will not issue new energy decrees for energy-intensive industries, clarifying that tariff decisions fall within ANDE's legal purview under its 1960s-era framework law. Peña emphasized the government's focus on generation capacity rather than consumption subsidies, in line with Paraguay's strategy to position itself as a destination for AI data centers and high-energy-demand industries. The Aña Cuá expansion will add 270 MW (10% increase to Yacyretá's output), with the first turbine operational in 2028. Peña also noted that Itaipú Annex C renegotiation is stalled pending Brazil's November 2026 elections.

events.title: IPS emergency: Senate evaluates USD 304M sovereign bond issuance to rescue social security system (2026-07-17)
events.summary: The Senate is evaluating modifications to the IPS (Social Security Institute) emergency bill, already approved by the Chamber of Deputies in May 2026. Proposed measures include issuing sovereign bonds of up to USD 304 million and securing multilateral loans to rescue the pension and healthcare system. The IPS faces a 40% medication shortage in Q1 2026 and deteriorating infrastructure. The emergency declaration reflects growing fiscal pressure from social security obligations, which Moody's has flagged as a medium-term risk to Paraguay's fiscal consolidation path.

events.title: MIC raises mandatory biodiesel blend to 8-10% in diesel, targeting USD 300M annual import savings (2026-07-17)
events.summary: The Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MIC) issued Resolution No. 472/2026 raising the mandatory biodiesel blend in regular diesel to between 8% and 10%, up from previous levels. The measure aims to reduce dependence on diesel imports and could generate annual foreign currency savings of up to USD 300 million. This aligns with the government's broader energy independence strategy, complementing the push for renewable electricity generation and the promotion of electric mobility.

sections.title: III. Social & Labor Developments
sections.description: Labor market, social stability, public security, employment data

events.title: New minimum wage takes effect July 1: Gs. 3,044,000/month, a 5% increase (2026-07-01)
events.summary: The new legal minimum wage for Paraguay's private sector took effect on July 1, 2026, under Decree No. 6225/2026, with a 5% increase based on CONASAM recommendations and the year-on-year CPI variation. The new monthly minimum is Gs. 3,044,000 (approximately USD 502 at the current exchange rate), with a daily minimum of Gs. 117,077. The MTESS was authorized to regulate and publish specific minimum wages for particular activities and scaled occupations.

events.title: Expo Empleo 2026 attracts over 2,000 job seekers for 1,410 positions across 40 companies (2026-07-17)
events.summary: The Expo Empleo ARP 2026, organized by MTESS in partnership with the Rural Association of Paraguay (ARP), attracted over 2,000 registrants for 1,410 job openings across 40 companies in sectors including pharmaceuticals, security, cleaning, retail, and industry. Over 9,000 online applications were received via the EmpleaPy platform. Salaries offered ranged from the minimum Gs. 3,044,000 to Gs. 6,500,000 depending on position and sector. A cooperation agreement was signed between MTESS, Sinafocal, and ARP to strengthen employability through training and labor competency certification.

events.title: Doctors announce nationwide strike for August; government pledges to protect critical services (2026-07-09)
events.summary: Medical professionals have announced a nationwide strike scheduled for August 2026, demanding improved working conditions, salary increases, and resolution of the IPS medication shortage. The Ministry of Health stated it will implement contingency plans to protect critical services during the strike. This labor action compounds existing pressures on Paraguay's healthcare system, which is already strained by the IPS emergency (40% medication deficit) and infrastructure deterioration.

sections.title: IV. International Relations & Diplomacy
sections.description: Paraguay's relations with major powers, Mercosur dynamics, cross-strait relations

events.title: Paraguay signals openness to China trade without cutting Taiwan ties; Beijing rejects conditional approach (2026-07-01)
events.summary: At the Mercosur Summit in Luque, Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez stated Paraguay is open to trade with China provided it is not required to sever diplomatic ties with Taiwan, declaring: 'If those are the conditions, we have no restrictions.' Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun immediately rejected this stance, urging Paraguay to 'stand on the right side of history' and adhere to the One China Principle. The Global Times (July 12) labeled the Paraguayan position as 'diplomatic opportunism,' stating the One China Principle is a 'non-negotiable red line.' Paraguay remains South America's only Taiwan ally and the sole Mercosur member without China relations. In parallel, Taiwan's Ambassador Ivan Lee inaugurated the Taiwan Pavilion at Expo Paraguay ARP 2026 on July 17, highlighting ongoing bilateral cooperation.

events.title: Mercosur Summit: Paraguay demands equal 25% distribution of EU meat quota; Uruguay assumes rotating presidency (2026-07-01)
events.summary: At the 68th Mercosur Summit in Asunción, President Santiago Peña firmly demanded an equal 25% distribution of EU tariff-rate quotas (particularly the 99,000-ton beef quota), calling it a 'matter of justice, not caprice,' noting that Paraguay as a landlocked country faces higher logistics costs that the current system fails to address. The dispute over sugar, beef, rice, and honey quotas remained unresolved. The summit marked the transfer of the rotating presidency from Paraguay to Uruguay and the bloc's 35th anniversary. Argentine President Javier Milei did not attend, sending his foreign minister instead. The EU-Mercosur FTA entered provisional application on May 1, 2026, but still requires ratification by the European Parliament and Mercosur legislatures. Germany acknowledged on July 1 that issues remain before EU ratification.

events.title: Mercosur launches trade negotiations with Japan, advances talks with UAE, Canada, and Vietnam (2026-07-01)
events.summary: During the Asunción summit, Mercosur leaders formally launched an economic partnership agreement negotiation with Japan (bilateral trade of USD 13.7 billion in 2025) and confirmed intentions to conclude FTAs with the UAE and Canada, with Vietnam's first round scheduled for H2 2026 in Buenos Aires. India trade preference deepening and EFTA implementation were also prioritized. The EU-Mercosur deal was explicitly framed as a bet on multilateralism against rising protectionism, particularly in the context of potential Trump-era tariffs. Spain's Secretary of State for Trade highlighted in Asunción on July 15 that the EU-Mercosur agreement opens a 'new stage for trade and investment,' identifying opportunities for Paraguay in reforestation, industrialization, and food production.

events.title: Taiwan-Paraguay 'Yguazú Digital' AI data center project advances with USD 200M Taiwanese financing (2026-07-06)
events.summary: The Taiwan-Paraguay 'Yguazú Digital' project, a 50-50 bilateral alliance to develop one of the world's largest AI data centers, is advancing with USD 200 million in Taiwanese financing. The center will start at 10 MW and scale to 1 GW (1,000 MW), with operations expected by end-2027. It is reportedly the world's first bilateral government plan to build AI computing infrastructure. The project is seen as a strategic deepening of Taiwan-Paraguay ties amid Beijing's diplomatic pressure on Asunción. The initiative also involves Paraguay's Taiwan-backed Parque Tecnológico Itaipú (PTI-PY) and is expected to catalyze broader investments in AI, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure.

sections.title: V. Industry Focus: Telecom, Digital Energy & AI
sections.description: 5G spectrum and commercial rollout, fiber infrastructure, digital energy investment, AI data centers, industry policy

events.title: Tigo and Personal bid in Paraguay's second 5G spectrum auction, committing USD 40M+ in infrastructure (2026-07-18)
events.summary: Tigo (Millicom) and Personal (Núcleo) submitted bids in CONATEL's second 5G spectrum auction (Licitación No. 01/2026), offering frequencies in the 2.3 GHz and 3.5 GHz bands. Both operators had abstained from the first 2025 auction over restrictions that effectively excluded Chinese vendors (Huawei, ZTE). The new auction requires a minimum USD 40 million investment in secure network infrastructure with trusted-vendor equipment compatible with 5G NR Release 15 or higher. This marks a major competitive shift: Paraguay's two largest mobile operators (Tigo: 3.16M users, Personal: 1.66M users) are now set to join Claro (947K users, 5G launched Dec 2025) in the 5G race. The auction also offers spectrum Claro did not acquire, including the 2.3 GHz band.

events.title: HIVE Digital Technologies expands Paraguay operations: 100MW substation near completion, Tier III data center planned (2026-07-18)
events.summary: HIVE Digital Technologies is accelerating its Paraguay expansion: a 100 MW substation in Yguazú has civil works completed with energization expected by September 2026, and construction of a new Tier III data center will begin in autumn 2026 with service readiness in H2 2027. HIVE currently operates approximately 300 MW in Tier I data centers in Paraguay and launched the BUZZ AI Cloud platform in Asunción (January 2026) targeting academic, healthcare, and enterprise clients. Paraguay's electricity costs — up to 2.8x cheaper than Brazil — and 100% renewable hydro matrix are key competitive advantages. The company's total Paraguay footprint positions it among the country's largest digital infrastructure investors.

events.title: Nubicom 5G deployment under investigation for non-compliance with USD 200M investment commitment (2026-07-18)
events.summary: Nubicom, the Argentine internet provider that won 200 MHz of 3.5 GHz spectrum in Paraguay's first 5G auction (August 2025) with a USD 200 million investment pledge, is under CONATEL investigation for failing to report any deployment progress. The company was required to establish a local subsidiary within six weeks and begin infrastructure deployment within six months, with commercial services expected by March-April 2026. Nubicom has no prior mobile network infrastructure in Argentina or Paraguay, making the USD 200M commitment particularly ambitious. The non-compliance raises questions about CONATEL's spectrum allocation oversight and may lead to spectrum revocation, potentially reopening the band to competing operators.

events.title: Aña Cuá expansion at 76% completion; will add 270 MW to Paraguay's grid, first turbine operational by 2028 (2026-07-17)
events.summary: The Aña Cuá expansion of the Yacyretá hydroelectric dam reached 76% physical completion as of President Peña's July 17 site visit. The project will add 270 MW of generation capacity (approximately 10% of Yacyretá's current output), with the first of three turbines scheduled to begin operations in 2028. The expansion is central to Paraguay's strategy of positioning itself as a clean energy hub for AI data centers and energy-intensive industries. Combined with Itaipú's existing capacity, the additional generation reinforces Paraguay's status as the world's largest per-capita electricity exporter, with the highest share of renewable electricity in South America.

events.title: Paraguay's fiber broadband market projected to grow at 5.7% CAGR to USD 289M by 2029; Tigo and Personal lead expansion (2026-03-12)
events.summary: Paraguay's fixed broadband services market is projected to grow from USD 219.3 million in 2024 to USD 289.1 million by 2029 (5.7% CAGR), driven by private investment in fiber-to-the-premises (FTTP) networks, national broadband targets, and expansion into underserved rural areas. Tigo (3.16M mobile internet users) and Personal (1.66M) are the primary operators driving fiber expansion, alongside COPACO (state-owned) and VOX. Despite 68% internet penetration, significant urban-rural connectivity gaps persist, presenting ongoing infrastructure investment opportunities. The mobile data segment is projected to reach USD 532.9 million by 2029 (3.9% CAGR from USD 440.6M in 2024).

sections.title: VI. Key Client Movements
sections.description: Tracking strategic repositioning, investment plans, network expansion, and technology choices of Paraguay's major telecom operators

events.title: Tigo (Millicom): Enters Paraguay 5G race with spectrum auction bid; market leader with 3.16M mobile users (2026-07-18)
events.summary: Tigo (Millicom) submitted a bid in Paraguay's second 5G spectrum auction, committing at least USD 40 million in secure network infrastructure. As the market leader with 3.16 million mobile internet users (+7% YoY) and the largest fiber network, Tigo's 5G entry significantly reshapes the competitive landscape. Tigo had previously abstained from the first auction over vendor restrictions excluding Huawei and ZTE. The operator is simultaneously expanding its fiber optic network to underserved rural areas and faces the challenge of defending market share against Claro's first-mover 5G advantage (launched Dec 2025). Millicom's broader Latin American strategy remains focused on connectivity infrastructure with investors watching long-term growth.

events.title: Personal (Núcleo): Bids for 5G spectrum while accelerating fiber expansion; 1.66M mobile users (2026-07-18)
events.summary: Personal (Núcleo), Paraguay's second-largest mobile operator with 1.66 million mobile internet users, submitted a bid alongside Tigo in the second 5G auction. Personal is simultaneously accelerating fiber optic network expansion to underserved areas, positioning itself for both mobile 5G and fixed broadband growth. The operator has been actively participating in the FTTP market, with GPON and EPON deployments aimed at closing the urban-rural connectivity gap. Personal's dual play (5G mobile + fiber broadband) positions it to capture growth across both segments, with the fixed broadband market projected to reach USD 289.1M by 2029.

events.title: Claro (América Móvil): 5G network operational since Dec 2025 with USD 35M initial investment; sustained expansion planned for 2026 (2026-03-12)
events.summary: Claro Paraguay, the first operator to launch commercial 5G services in the country (December 2025), continues its network expansion with an initial USD 35 million investment. Coverage spans Gran Asunción, Ciudad del Este, Encarnación, Coronel Oviedo, and Pedro Juan Caballero. The operator holds 200 MHz in the 3.5 GHz band (acquired for USD 2M) and partnered with Nokia for 5G radio and Massive MIMO equipment. However, Claro remains the third-largest operator with only 947,000 mobile internet users, and faces intensifying competition as Tigo and Personal now enter the 5G market through the second auction. Claro's general manager Alfredo Alcaraz stated 'sustained expansion to cover more of the national territory' is planned through 2026.

events.title: Nubicom: USD 200M 5G investment pledge under investigation for non-compliance; no deployment progress reported (2026-07-18)
events.summary: Nubicom, the Argentine fixed-wireless provider that won 200 MHz of 3.5 GHz spectrum in Paraguay's first 5G auction with an ambitious USD 200 million deployment pledge, faces a CONATEL investigation for failing to report any infrastructure deployment progress. The company was required to establish a local subsidiary (within six weeks) and begin deployment (within six months), with commercial services expected by March-April 2026. Nubicom has no prior mobile network experience, and its failure to execute raises significant counterparty risk. CONATEL may revoke the spectrum allocation, potentially freeing the 3.3-3.5 GHz band for reallocation to Tigo or Personal, who are bidding in the second auction. The situation underscores the execution risks associated with new-entrant operators in capital-intensive 5G deployments.

sections.title: VII. Comprehensive Impact Analysis for Business Operations
sections.description: Integrating macro, policy, industry, and client developments to assess enterprise impact across cost, market, and compliance dimensions
sections.impact_analysis:
**Macro Environment: Broadly Favorable with Fiscal Watchpoints**

Paraguay's macroeconomic fundamentals remain strong entering H2 2026. The BCP's upgraded 4.5% GDP growth forecast and Moody's Baa3 affirmation (third consecutive year) provide a stable and predictable environment for business planning. The guaraní's continued strength (PYG 6,060/USD, -8.5% YTD) benefits importers of equipment and technology — a tailwind for telecom infrastructure investment — while pressuring export-oriented sectors. Private credit expanding at 15.3% YoY signals healthy financial intermediation supporting business investment.

However, two fiscal risks require monitoring: (1) DNIT's H1 revenue growth of only 2.1% vs. the 9% budget target suggests potential fiscal tightening in H2 that could affect public procurement and infrastructure spending; (2) the IPS emergency and potential USD 304M bond issuance add contingent liabilities to the sovereign balance sheet, though Moody's assessment suggests these are manageable within the current rating. The IMF's warning on domestic arrears (USD 1.2B+) indicates unresolved structural fiscal pressures that could eventually affect the business environment through higher taxes or reduced public investment.

**Political & Regulatory: Pro-Investment with Emerging Oversight**

The policy environment remains strongly pro-investment, as evidenced by the Investor Pass program, the railway sector opening to international capital (Law 7665/2026, USD 480M Phase I with UAE's Etihad Rail), and maintained Maquila regime incentives. However, Congress's July 16 request for detailed reports on tech investment incentives and critical minerals strategy signals increasing legislative oversight of foreign investment, particularly in strategic sectors (data centers, mining, AI infrastructure). This is not yet restrictive but suggests the regulatory framework is evolving toward greater transparency requirements.

Peña's stated decision to not issue new energy decrees is a mixed signal: it provides regulatory stability (no unpredictable tariff changes) but also means new market entrants cannot negotiate bespoke electricity rates, relying instead on ANDE's standard framework. For energy-intensive projects (data centers, AI computing), this may slow deal-making compared to the previous environment.

**Industry Dynamics: 5G Competition Intensifying — A Window for Equipment and Infrastructure Providers**

The entry of Tigo and Personal into the 5G auction marks a structural shift in Paraguay's telecom market. After Claro's solo 5G launch in December 2025, the market is moving toward a three-operator 5G landscape, which will drive:
- Accelerated infrastructure investment (minimum USD 40M per operator in the auction alone, plus deployment costs)
- Increased demand for trusted-vendor 5G equipment (Nokia already supplying Claro; Tigo/Personal vendor choices TBD)
- Fiber backhaul expansion to support 5G densification
- Potential for network sharing or infrastructure collaboration to manage deployment costs

Nubicom's non-compliance investigation is a cautionary tale but also creates opportunity: if its 200 MHz of 3.5 GHz spectrum is revoked and reallocated, the competitive dynamics could shift further. Equipment vendors and infrastructure service providers should closely track the auction outcome and subsequent vendor selection processes.

**Digital Infrastructure: Paraguay Positioning as Regional AI Hub — But Execution Gaps Remain**

The convergence of Taiwan's USD 200M Yguazú Digital commitment, HIVE's 100MW substation + Tier III data center, and the Aña Cuá 270MW expansion creates credible momentum for Paraguay as a regional AI/compute hub. However, key gaps persist:
- Grid capacity limited to approximately 5 GW constrains the scale of announced projects (X8 Cloud's USD 50B/30-year vision appears aspirational)
- No specific data center regulatory framework exists yet
- Itaipú Annex C renegotiation (stalled until after Brazil's November 2026 elections) creates uncertainty about long-term electricity pricing
- Human capital shortages in AI, engineering, and data center operations

Businesses in digital infrastructure should treat announced figures with appropriate skepticism while recognizing the genuine structural advantages (cheap renewable power, strategic location, government backing).

sections.title: VIII. China-Specific Risk Assessment & Recommendations
sections.description: Special risk and opportunity analysis for Chinese enterprises, including policy risk, diplomatic risk, and business recommendations
sections.impact_analysis:
**Diplomatic Environment: Elevated Friction with No Near-Term Resolution**

The diplomatic standoff between Paraguay and China intensified in this period. Paraguay's July 1 proposal for trade-without-recognition was categorically rejected by Beijing, with the Global Times labeling Paraguay's position 'diplomatic opportunism.' The Chinese Consulate in São Paulo's mid-July statement rejecting Paraguay-US cyber-activity accusations added another layer of tension. For Chinese enterprises, the core constraint remains unchanged: the absence of diplomatic relations means no bilateral investment treaty (BIT) protection, no preferential trade access, and potential political headwinds for high-profile investments.

**However, the window is not closed.** Paraguay's export-oriented sectors (particularly agriculture) increasingly advocate for China market access. The Mercosur's push to diversify trade partners — including negotiations with Japan, UAE, and Vietnam — reflects a broader regional rebalancing that could indirectly benefit Chinese commercial interests. Chinese enterprises with strong local partnerships and non-sensitive sector focus (infrastructure, renewable energy equipment, EV supply chain) can still operate in Paraguay, leveraging the country's open investment regime and Maquila incentives.

**🔴 High-Risk Factors:**
- Direct government procurement contracts face political vetting risk
- Telecom equipment (Huawei, ZTE) remains effectively excluded from 5G deployment under CONATEL's trusted-vendor requirements in the second auction
- High-profile greenfield investments may attract diplomatic scrutiny from both Taipei and Washington
- No BIT protection means dispute resolution relies on contractual provisions and Paraguayan courts

**🟡 Medium-Risk / Monitoring Items:**
- Congress's July 16 request for tech investment reports could lead to sector-specific foreign investment review mechanisms
- The critical minerals strategy (lithium, titanium, rare earths) represents a potential opportunity but also a sensitive sector where Chinese involvement would draw geopolitical attention
- Itaipú Annex C renegotiation outcome (post-November 2026) will affect long-term electricity pricing for data center investments

**🟢 Opportunities:**
- Fiber optic and broadband infrastructure equipment supply (not subject to the same vendor restrictions as 5G RAN)
- Renewable energy equipment (solar panels, wind turbines, battery storage) for Paraguay's non-hydro renewable push under Decree 6034
- EV and electric mobility supply chain (MIC's biodiesel mandate signals openness to energy transition)
- Data center construction and cooling infrastructure (civil works, electrical systems) — less politically sensitive than AI computing layer
- Agricultural technology and machinery (Paraguay's record soybean harvest underscores agtech demand)

**Strategic Recommendations:**

【Immediate】
- Avoid direct bidding on government-procured telecom or critical infrastructure projects; prioritize B2B and private-sector opportunities
- Monitor the outcome of the second 5G auction and Tigo/Personal vendor selection processes — this will clarify whether the trusted-vendor framework may evolve
- Map Paraguay's fiber broadband expansion plans as a near-term equipment supply opportunity

【Short-Term (1-3 months)】
- Explore partnership models with existing operators (Tigo, Personal, Claro) for equipment supply, managed services, or infrastructure sharing — operational partnerships face fewer political barriers than direct market entry
- Assess participation in Paraguay's non-hydro renewable energy supply chain (solar, storage) under Decree 6034
- Track Congressional tech investment report outcomes (due within weeks of July 16 request) for early signals of regulatory changes

【Medium-Term (3-12 months)】
- Prepare for potential Taiwan-Paraguay diplomatic evolution — any shift would rapidly transform the operating environment for Chinese enterprises
- Evaluate Maquila-regime manufacturing opportunities (1% tax on value-added) for equipment assembly or component production serving the Brazilian and Southern Cone markets
- Position for Itaipú Annex C renegotiation outcome: if Paraguay secures higher electricity sale prices to Brazil, the domestic tariff structure may become more favorable for industrial consumers
